subject: Post-demo: geo latency + hyperscaler comparison — proposed checklist & next tests
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: John Donovan <john.donovan@medsys.ai>, Sara Li <sara.li@cloudcorp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 28 Jul 2026 15:10:00 -0400
Subject: Post-demo: geo latency + hyperscaler comparison — proposed checklist & next tests

John / Sara — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we’re all aligned.

What we covered (short):
- MedSys production goals: <10% 95p latency >150ms for document-processing flows, EU data residency required for clinical records, failover to US region for analytics.
- Primary competitors you’re evaluating: CloudCorp managed endpoints (Sara), and a self-hosted inference run from EdgeProbe (bench demos).
- Key decision criteria: live latency from EU/US, model quality on your prompt sets, cost per 1M tokens at 98% availability, and controls for data residency & audit logs.

Proposed next tests (agreeable to run this week):
1) Head-to-head latency runs from EU and US: 1K requests each region, P50/P95/P99, and payload distribution (short/long docs).
2) Cold-start + KV-cache test: simulating bursty queries with and without prefix caching (50 sessions).
3) Throughput burn: sustained 2k rps for 10 minutes to validate autoscale and 95th latency.
4) Security/compliance check: show audit log export and KMS integration options for EU region.

What we (Redwood) will provide:
- Test harness + script (runs via EdgeProbe agents or your test VMs), a comparison matrix vs CloudCorp and EdgeProbe, and a proposed Dedicated capacity SKU for MedSys. Attached: Redwood comparison matrix + runbook.

Asks for MedSys:
- Confirm EU availability test locations (Frankfurt, Amsterdam, London?) and whether test traffic must exit the EU.
- Share two representative prompt files (short/long) and a sample request rate for peak window.

Next steps / timeline:
- Rishi: coordinate test window and hand off harness to Marissa. (Today)
- Marissa: run the tests and share raw samples + summary. (within 48 hours once harness confirmed)
- Neha: prepare pricing for Dedicated + Private options and data residency add-on. (2 business days)

Thanks — I’ll queue the harness as soon as you confirm the EU nodes.

—
Rishi Malhotra
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0142

Attachments referenced: redwood-hyperscaler-comparison-matrix.pdf, geo-latency-sample-runbook.md

From: John Donovan <john.donovan@medsys.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 29 Jul 2026 09:45:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-demo: geo latency + hyperscaler comparison — proposed checklist & next tests

Rishi — this is great, thanks for the clear recap. Confirming a few items from our side: 

- EU endpoints: Frankfurt and Amsterdam would be ideal; we need to ensure all patient PHI stays in-region for the clinical ingestion pipeline. For analytics/ranking we can failover to US.
- Prompt files: attaching two sample payloads (short_summary.json, long_transcript.json).
- Peak pattern: typical peak is ~800 rps sustained over 10–15 minutes during nightly ingestion windows, occasional 2k rps bursts for batch jobs.

A couple of clarifying questions:
1) For the head-to-head with CloudCorp — can you produce per-token cost estimates using our peak/burst profile?
2) For the Private/VPC option, what parts of the control plane stay in our VPC vs Redwood control plane? We need specifics for our security review.

We’re happy to have EdgeProbe run its agents from our EU VMs if that helps with parity. Looping Sara from CloudCorp since they asked to see the schedule for a short benchmark (Sara: no objection if it’s transparent).

Thanks — John
John Donovan
Head of Data Platform | MedSys
john.donovan@medsys.ai | +44 20 7123 9812

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: John Donovan <john.donovan@medsys.ai>
Date: Wed, 29 Jul 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: ACTION: run geo head-to-head (EU/US) + pricing draft for MedSys (DEAL-2026-034)

Marissa / Neha — following John’s confirmation and the attached sample payloads, please prioritize the following: 

Marissa (runbooks & runs):
- Use the attached runbook (geo-latency-sample-runbook.md) and spin tests from Frankfurt and Amsterdam as primary EU nodes, plus Virginia for US. If MedSys prefers London instead of Amsterdam, swap as directed in the runbook.
- Tests to run: 1k synthetic requests per node (mix of short/long), cold-start + KV-cache toggle, and a 10-min 2k-rps throughput burn from US node to validate autoscale behavior.
- Produce: CSV of per-request latencies (P50/P95/P99), token counts, and raw traces. Zip and upload to the shared drive link; mark results with run tags.
- ETA: start within 24 hours after you confirm VM access (John will provide), deliver initial results inside 48 hrs.

Neha (pricing & security):
- Draft a comparative pricing table for Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private deployment for MedSys profile (use peak/burst numbers John provided). Include rough costs for reserved capacity and expected per-token cost at their 2k-burst level.
- Prepare a short control-plane diagram and a bulleted summary: what remains in Redwood control plane vs customer VPC for Private deployment (KMS, audit logs, model artifacts residency, telemetry). We need to answer: does any request metadata leave EU?
- ETA: pricing + control plane summary in 2 business days.

John — cc’ing you so you can see the plan. Please send VM access instructions (or confirm EdgeProbe agent access) and any additional constraints (e.g., IP allowlists).

Rishi

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: John Donovan <john.donovan@medsys.ai>, EdgeProbe Diagnostics <partners@edgeprobe.io>
Date: Sat, 01 Aug 2026 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: RE: ACTION: run geo head-to-head (EU/US) + pricing draft for MedSys (DEAL-2026-034)

All — status update and attached artifacts.

What we ran (completed):
- 1K requests from Frankfurt, 1K from Amsterdam, 1K from Virginia (us-east-1) using John’s short/long payloads. Each run recorded P50/P95/P99 and token counts.
- Cold-start vs warmed KV-cache toggle included (100 sessions per region).
- Throughput burn: 10-minute 2k-rps from Virginia to validate autoscale; observed autoscale window ~45s and sustained 98p availability.

Key results (summary):
- EU (Frankfurt): P50 85ms / P95 230ms / P99 410ms (short payloads).
- EU (Amsterdam): P50 90ms / P95 245ms / P99 425ms (short).
- US (Virginia): P50 60ms / P95 160ms / P99 300ms (short).
- Cold-starts increased P95 by ~180ms on average. Warmed-KV sessions reduced per-token CPU by ~12% and P95 by ~40ms.

Attached: us-eu-latency-samples.csv (raw), redwood-hyperscaler-comparison-matrix.pdf (matrix with CloudCorp and EdgeProbe numbers), and a short runbook.

Notes / next asks:
- Neha, I flagged a couple of pricing scenarios in the matrix (reserved Dedicated vs burst pricing). Please confirm recommended SKU and the two-tier data residency add-on.
- John: results show we can meet your P95 goal in the US comfortably; EU P95 is slightly above target for long documents — options: a) pin a higher-capacity Dedicated pool in EU, b) enable a quantized model variant with lower latency (possible quality delta), or c) accept EU warm-KV priming before peak windows.

I’m happy to walk through the CSV and matrix on a quick call; otherwise I’ll slot a follow up with John for Monday.

—
Marissa Cole
Platform Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0181
